# Collegica as an OKF wiki — design and proof of concept

How the human site at collegica.org becomes readable by agents as an [Open
Knowledge Format](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md)
v0.2 bundle, without authoring anything twice. Started 2026-09-12. The proof
of concept covers the Finance subject; the projection generalises.

## What OKF is, in one paragraph

A directory of markdown files with YAML frontmatter. One required key,
`type`. Optional families for **provenance** (`sources`, with ids so a footnote
can attribute a claim), **trust** (`generated` — who wrote it; `verified` —
who confirmed it; the two are deliberately distinct), **lifecycle** (`status`,
`stale_after`), and **attested computations** (a sanctioned computation with
typed parameters, an executor that returns a receipt, and a deterministic
attester that checks it). `index.md` is a reserved listing for progressive
disclosure; `log.md` a reserved history. Conformance is minimal: every
non-reserved `.md` has parseable frontmatter with a non-empty `type`. Consumers
must tolerate unknown types, unknown keys, broken links and missing indexes.

## The finding that shaped the design

Collegica already *practises* what OKF's fields formalise, in prose:

| OKF field | Where the site already does it |
|---|---|
| `sources` with per-claim ids | Every article's Sources section, with dates |
| Trust tiers: unverified / machine-confirmed / human-reviewed | The "Access and confidence" section opening every research note — *read in full / snippet-only / not verified* is the same three-way split |
| `generated.by` ≠ `verified.by` | Articles drafted by an agent, reviewed line by line by a person; OKF makes that first-class |
| `stale_after` | "Checked on 12 September 2026 — rates move daily" |
| Attested Computation | `mortgage.js` + `rates.json` + `build.mjs`: a sanctioned computation with typed parameters that regenerates the article's own tables |

The audit: 45 content files. 24 carry Quarto frontmatter (no `type`, `sources`
or `verified` anywhere). 21 carry none — and those include the richest material
for an agent: all twelve research notes (59,000 words), the app specs, the video
READMEs.

## Decisions

1. **One source of truth, generated bundle.** Source files stay byte-identical.
   A script projects `website/`, `docs/` and `video/` into `okf/`, which is
   committed (so `git clone` works, the spec's preferred distribution) *and*
   copied into `public/okf/` on every deploy (so `GET /okf/index.md` works).
2. **Judgement fields live in a sidecar**, `okf/manifest.yml`, not in article
   frontmatter. This honours the standing rule that existing articles are not
   edited, and keeps the fields that require a human decision — `type`, who
   verified what and when, when a fact goes stale — in one reviewable file.
   Timestamps are never typed by hand: `at: git:<path-or-ref>` resolves to a
   commit date.
3. **The Quarto `index.qmd` / OKF `index.md` collision is resolved in the
   generator**: subject landing pages are already listings, so their prose
   becomes the directory description and their links become the listing.
4. **Attestation is real, not decorative.** The mortgage computation ships with
   an executor that prints a receipt (hashes of the code and data that ran, the
   bound parameters, the result) and an attester that re-hashes, re-runs and
   compares. Tested: it attests honest runs and rejects a changed number, a
   swapped computation, and a smuggled parameter.
5. **Discovery via `llms.txt`** at the site root, pointing at the bundle index.
6. **Squash-proof timestamps.** A first cut dated concepts from the last commit
   touching their source file. That drifts: a squash merge or rebase rewrites
   commit dates, so the committed bundle would disagree with a fresh projection
   on `main` after every merge. Defaults are now content-derived — an article's
   own `date:`, a research folder's `YYYY-MM-DD-` prefix — and `git:` is
   reserved for explicit SHAs on `main`, which never move. Verified by amending
   a commit (which moves its date) and regenerating: byte-identical.
7. **Honest actors.** Nearly everything in the Finance bundle was drafted by
   `claude/opus-5` and reviewed by `human:behzad`; the manifest says so, per
   concept, and the research notes — which were not reviewed line by line —
   carry no `verified` and therefore sit in the *unverified* tier. That is the
   correct tier, and the point of having tiers.

## What the proof of concept contains

Twelve concepts, all conformant, every in-bundle link resolving:

```
okf/
  index.md                       okf_version: "0.2"; sections
  log.md
  manifest.yml                   the sidecar (producer config, not a concept)
  finance/
    fixed-or-variable.md         Article — human-reviewed twice, stale after the next BoC decision
    fixed-or-variable-video.md   Video
    research/                    Research Report + 3 Research Notes (auto-harvested sources)
    computations/mortgage.md     Attested Computation — runtime node, 4 typed parameters
    newsletter/                  3 References to the human-authored companion pieces
  references/
    data/rates.md + rates.json   Dataset — schema lifted from the JSON's own `_` notes
    computations/mortgage.js     the computation, copied verbatim, hashed in the concept
    executors/run-compare.{md,mjs}
    attesters/mortgage-attester.mjs
```

The projection handles what Quarto puts in a body: fenced divs are unwrapped,
callouts become blockquotes with a bold title, `{=html}` blocks and
`{{< include >}}` shortcodes are replaced by manifest-supplied text (a link to
the video concept, a figure caption pointing at the dataset, a pointer from the
browser-only calculator to the attested computation), table captions keep
their text and lose their attributes, and links to the GitHub repo or to
relative source paths are rewritten into bundle-relative edges.

## Running it

```bash
pixi run okf        # regenerate okf/ from okf/manifest.yml and the source tree
pixi run public     # …which now also copies okf/ into public/okf/
```

```bash
# run the computation and check the run — Node 18+, no packages
node okf/references/executors/run-compare.mjs --start 2021-09 --term 5 \
  | node okf/references/attesters/mortgage-attester.mjs
```

`python` and `pyyaml` were added to `pixi.toml` for the generator, which is
the first Python this repository has needed — appropriately, three days after
the Python track argued that environments are what you pin.

## What the generator does not do, deliberately

- **It does not invent trust.** A concept with no `verified` in the manifest
  has no `verified` in the bundle. The research notes are unverified because
  nobody has verified them.
- **It does not print what could not be checked.** The same discipline as the
  articles: no funder policy dates, no snippet-grade figures promoted to
  fact.
- **It does not delete.** It overwrites the files it owns; a concept removed
  from the manifest leaves its old file behind until someone removes it. Fine
  for a PoC; a `--prune` flag is the obvious next step.
- **It does not resolve `git:` dates for uncommitted files.** They get the
  current time and a warning on stderr — which is what `manifest.yml` itself
  got on its first run, and is correct.

## Python, added 2026-09-12

The second subject, and the first test of the claim that the generator does
not change per subject. It did not. Nine concepts joined: two articles, the two
2023 pieces (a `Guide` and `Slides`, human-authored and human-verified), the
research report and two notes, `bocrates` as a second Attested Computation
with a **Python** runtime, its CSV as a Dataset, and this document as `about`.

Two things the projection handles that Finance did not need: `{{< video >}}`
shortcodes become a link to the recorded talk, and image and `/slides/` links
are rewritten to absolute site URLs. The example project is carried as a
runnable nine-file tree under `references/computations/bocrates/`, without its
README — a markdown file with no frontmatter would break §11 conformance, so
the concept is its description.

`bocrates` sits in the **machine-confirmed** tier: `verified: { by:
process:pytest }`, because its five-test suite ran green before the article
was written. With the Finance article human-reviewed and the research notes
unverified, all three trust tiers now appear in the bundle, each for the
honest reason.

Two bugs found by the checks and fixed before anything shipped:

- **A rounded receipt failed an honest attestation.** The Python executor
  rounded each mean to six decimals; the attester compared at 1e-9. A receipt
  is evidence and must carry the exact value — the executor no longer rounds.
- **A prose mention of a shortcode was treated as one.** This document says
  `{{< include >}}` in a sentence; the generator's shortcode matcher dropped
  the line mid-sentence. Real shortcodes sit alone on a line, and the matcher
  now requires that.

## Aging well and the app specs, added 2026-09-12

Fifteen concepts: the three articles, their three videos, the next-job
research report and its four notes, the OWL Planner as an `Application`
pointing at its own repository, and the three app specifications as
`status: draft`. The next-job article is **human-reviewed** — the clarity
corrections applied in PR #19 are a recorded review event, pinned to that
merge. The other two were unverified until the author approved them later
the same day — at which point the flip was the one-line manifest edit the
design promised, with the approval instant recorded as `verified.at`.

New projection cases, all checked in the output: anchored cross-links keep
their fragments; `/owl/` and `/slides/` become site URLs; a research
README's bare `notes/` link resolves to the research directory while every
specific note keeps its own mapping, because keys match longest-first; and
the site's own static media is never harvested as a "source" when a
video-banner replacement mentions it.

The bundle now spans four subjects and 38 concepts, all from one generator
that has not needed a subject-specific branch.

## Using the bundle with Claude

Three tiers, from zero setup to proper integration.

1. **Point Claude at the URL.** In claude.ai with web fetch on, or in Claude
   Code: *"Read https://www.collegica.org/llms.txt and answer from the OKF
   bundle it points to."* Tested: Claude fetched the mortgage computation
   concept cold and read the type, actors, staleness, runtime, parameters and
   the exact run-then-attest sequence from its frontmatter alone. The limit is
   that a chat can read the attested computations but cannot run them.

2. **Claude Code in this repository — the `/okf` skill.**
   `.claude/skills/okf/SKILL.md` teaches a session to consume the bundle
   properly: start at `okf/index.md`, resolve bundle-relative links, read the
   frontmatter first, name the trust tier with every answer, refuse figures
   past `stale_after`, attribute by `sources[].id`, and — the part that
   matters — **run the attested computations and quote the receipt rather than
   the article**, with the exact commands for both. It also carries the rules
   for keeping the bundle current (regenerate after editing a source; edit the
   manifest, never a generated file) and the trap of rounding before
   subtracting. Validated: every path it names exists, all three command
   blocks attest as written, and its worked example matches the receipt.
   Claude Code discovers project skills at session start, so a session already
   open when the file lands must be restarted to see it.

   **A public version of the same skill lives in the bundle itself**, at
   `okf/references/skills/collegica/SKILL.md` — served at
   https://www.collegica.org/okf/references/skills/collegica/SKILL.md and
   linked from the front page and `llms.txt`. It is an OKF concept
   (`type: Skill`, the spec's own `references/skills/` convention) *and* a
   valid Claude Code skill: the extra frontmatter keys are ignored by the
   skill loader and tolerated by OKF consumers. It differs from `/okf` in one
   essential way: it must work for someone with nothing but the URL, so every
   path is a fetch from collegica.org, and the attested computations are run
   by first fetching the executor, attester, computation and data into the
   `references/` layout they ship in. Install:
   `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/collegica && curl -sSL <that URL> -o ~/.claude/skills/collegica/SKILL.md`,
   restart, `/collegica`.

3. **An MCP server** exposing `list_concepts`, `get_concept`, and
   `run_computation` returning an attested receipt — the integration OKF's
   executor/attester contract is designed for, and the right answer once
   agents outside this repository need the bundle. Not built; the
   `knowledge-catalog` repository's README documents no consumer of its own.

## Extending to the rest of the site

Remaining, in rough order of value to an agent:

1. **Talks and events** — `type: Talk` / `type: Event`, `resource` pointing at
   the deck; the slide sources under `slides/` and the event flyer.
2. **Software** — the newsletter references on `software.qmd`, and the
   reproducibility talk.
3. **The home, about and subject pages** — mostly listings already; a
   directory description each.

Two conventions to settle before scaling further: how a note's prose "Access
and confidence" section maps onto `sources[]` credibility signals (today the
generator harvests every URL; it does not yet tag which were read in full), and
whether new articles carry OKF fields natively in their own frontmatter so the
sidecar only covers the back catalogue.

## Open questions
- ~~CI does not check that the committed `okf/` matches a fresh run.~~ It
  does now: the workflow checks out full history (the `git:` SHAs need it) and
  fails if `okf/` differs from a fresh projection, so `git clone` and
  `GET /okf/` cannot disagree. The squash-proof dates above are what make that
  check viable.
- **Model actor naming.** `claude/opus-5` follows the `<producer>/<version>`
  convention from the commit trailers of the period. Later work in this session
  carries a different trailer; the manifest should track whichever the commit
  says.
